messages:
neil: Heads-up: zephyr-mini-int8 canary shows duplicated tool invocations when streaming cuts off before final token. Small but dangerous for side-effecting tools.

maria: can you paste a minimal trace?

neil: sure:
```
chunkA: '{"action": "call", "name": "send_email", "args": {"to": "x@ex.com"'
chunkB: ', "body": "hi"}}'
chunkC: <lost>  <-- final token lost
parser: EOFError -> runtime retry -> duplicate email sent
```

ashley: two low-effort mitigations: 1) small quiesce on EOF parse failures (derive from chunk_gap p95), 2) parser emits partial_funccall flag when it sees action==call+name, and runtime suppresses auto-retry if flag set.

maria: prefer both: quiesce to catch late frames, flag to avoid unsafe retries. Which percentiles do we have?

infra-bot: telemetry: zephyr-mini-canary chunk_gap_ms p50=16 p95=95 p99=210.

neil: given p99=210, start quiesce=250ms for canary. We'll A/B down if latency hit.

eval-bot: canary test plan: 5k synthetic streaming requests, inject tail-frame-loss at 0.8% of traces. Compare baseline, quiesce-250ms, flag-only, and combined. Metrics: dup_toolcalls_per_100k, parse_fail_rate, added_latency_p95.

maria: owners?

ashley: I'll add parser flag and unit fuzz.

neil: I'll wire quiesce and RequestState.side_effect flag into retry scheduler. Add trace field 'retry_suppressed_by_flag'.

maria: acceptance: combined reduces dup invocations by >=90% w/o parse-failure regress >0.1%. I'll open RFC and dashboard ticket.
